items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Charlie Antolini was the drummer and he could swing.

ctx.x: I left Paris for Zurich the 27th of February rehearsed with the orchestra the 28th and we did our first date the first of March in Lugano, in the Italian part of Switzerland. Other places we played in Switzerland were Bellinzona, Ascona, Grenchen, Winterthur, Basel, Luzern, Schaffausen, Bern and Uster. The pianist with the Tremble Kids Orchestra was a young Swedish fellow named Ola Ringstrom who had a good swinging style.

The leader of the band was a clarinetist named Verner Keller. A good and lively musician. The trumpet man was named Oscar Klein and he also played guitar. Oscar was a real solid dixieland trumpeter and his style reminded me very much of Wild Bill Davison. I never knew Oscar's nationality but I think he was from Austria. Rolf Eizmek was the bass man and Charlie Antolini was the drummer and he could swing. I give the reader of this book the privilege of choosing whatever nationality they may think these last two…

The tour of Switzerland finished the 10th of March. The 12th we were in Wuppertal, Germany, the next night in Dusseldorf and the following night in Dortmund. From Dortmund we jumped to Linz in Austria the 15th followed by a concert in Vienna the 16th and the 18th in Salzburg.
